To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the biomass of petioles and laminae of the annual grass E. crus-galli was allocated in such a manner as to maximize the capture of light, (ii) the biomass allocation pattern was adjusted to the light environment, and (iii) the biomass allocation between the laminae and petioles of E. crus-galliw as a function of the light environment was similar to that of a theoretical model.

(1) petioles are important organs in the game of light competition between plants, (2) the biomass allocated to petioles is a good predictor of the light interception of a plant and of its competitive ability, and (3) petiole biomass is a good proxy for petiole length.
the biomass allocation pattern between petioles and lamina is a critical factor for light competition in a densely populated stand of an annual herb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of biomass allocation in a dense stand in a game of competitive light acquisition.
how plants allocate biomass among different organs, and how this allocation affects the competitive interactions between neighbouring plants.
how plants allocate biomass among lamina and petiolar tissues in a game of shade-avoidance and light competition in dense annual plant populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of petioles is a very important factor that affects the growth, development and survival of plants.

the role of petioles in light competition in dense plant stands is to provide the laminae with a greater opportunity to intercept light, and that petiole length is a key determinant in the success of the plants in a light competition game.
the allocation pattern of lamina and petiolar biomass is the most important factor determining the outcome of the game of light competition between neighbouring plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that petiole biomass allocation is a major factor determining competitive ability in dense populations of an annual herb (Erodium cicaturium), which is a species with a high petiole:lamina mass ratio (PLM).

biomass allocation between laminae and petioles is an adaptive response of the plants in a dense stand to the competition for light, and that it is a key factor in determining the growth rate of the plants in the stand.
the allocation to petiole biomass is a key determinant in a game of competition for light.
The main takeaway from our work is that
petioles play an important role in the game of light competition.
the petiole can play an important role in light capture and allocation in dense plant stands.
the petiole of a leaf is not a passive structure, but rather an active component that plays a key role in light interception and light competition.
